name: Carbamazepine
route_note: Oral tablets, chewable and extended-release tablets/capsules and suspension; suppositories in some countries and an IV formulation (Carnexiv) in the US.
targets: Voltage-gated sodium channels (SCN1A, SCN2A and others)

discovery.note: Synthesised during work on tricyclic compounds related to imipramine; anticonvulsant and anti-neuralgic effects were recognised around 1962.

tagline: First-line drug for trigeminal neuralgia and a long-standing focal epilepsy treatment
summary: Carbamazepine is a tricyclic anticonvulsant used for focal and tonic-clonic seizures, trigeminal neuralgia and bipolar disorder. It is effective and inexpensive but induces its own metabolism and many drug interactions, and carries a genetic risk of severe skin reactions.
mechanism: Carbamazepine stabilises inactivated voltage-gated sodium channels, reducing high-frequency repetitive firing of neurons and synaptic propagation of seizure discharges.
In trigeminal neuralgia it suppresses abnormal ectopic firing of damaged trigeminal afferents. Its active metabolite carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide contributes to both efficacy and toxicity.
uses: Acute mania and bipolar disorder (extended-release, Equetro)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Walter Schindler synthesises carbamazepine at Geigy in Basel.

history.title: Trigeminal neuralgia
history.detail: Blom reports efficacy in trigeminal neuralgia.

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Tegretol is marketed in Switzerland and soon the UK for epilepsy.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Tegretol, initially for trigeminal neuralgia; the epilepsy indication follows in 1974.

history.title: Bipolar disorder
history.detail: Equetro is approved in the US for acute manic and mixed episodes.

history.title: HLA-B*1502 boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA recommends genetic screening for HLA-B*15:02 in patients of Asian ancestry before starting therapy.

pk.half_life: about 25–65 hours after a single dose, falling to 12–17 hours with repeated dosing (autoinduction)
pk.metabolism: hepatic, mainly CYP3A4, to the active 10,11-epoxide; strong enzyme inducer

safety.boxed_warning: Serious dermatologic reactions including SJS/TEN, strongly associated with HLA-B*1502 (test at-risk patients before treatment); aplastic anaemia and agranulocytosis.

facts: Carbamazepine's dibenzazepine structure is closely related to the tricyclic antidepressant imipramine.
Oxcarbazepine and eslicarbazepine were developed as relatives that avoid the epoxide metabolite.
